evidence.supportingExcerpt: A synthetic cytokine receptor is an engineered cell-surface protein that connects a specified input to intracellular signalling. It differs from engineering a soluble cytokine or simply administering a cytokine. Some designs require an externally supplied ligand; others generate ligand-independent signalling. A growth-supporting signal does not itself establish antigen recognition, entry into a tumour, completed killing or durable patient benefit.

Engelowski and colleagues joined fluorescent-protein-binding nanobodies to selected cytokine-receptor membrane and intracellular domains. Artificial GFP/mCherry-based ligands induced signalling in experimental systems. That 2018 study is a particular ligand-dependent design, not a test of every synthetic receptor or of a company platform with a different architecture.

In a 2010 human T-cell study, a chimeric receptor joined the IL-4 receptor binding region to an IL-2/IL-15 receptor signalling component. IL-4 supported expansion of the engineered cells, while a separate CAR specified the tumour target. The reported culture experiments distinguished expansion, cytokine dependence and target-cell killing; they were not patient efficacy results.

Read each supportive feature as a testable hypothesis. A drug-triggered signal needs a baseline and a withdrawal test; an antigen-triggered signal needs testing after cells leave the priming site. Constitutive signalling raises different growth and cell-state questions, while a secreted payload can affect neighbouring cells or circulate. Orthogonal means sufficiently separate from natural partners under tested conditions, not selectivity established by its name. The supportive receptor does not specify the CAR target, and changing an internal signal is different from secreting a cytokine. An added support signal does not by itself demonstrate adequate oxygen, tissue access, recognition of an absent antigen or patient benefit.

semanticAssessment.explanation: Defined artificial ligand/receptor experiments and human-cell IL-4 expansion support selected signalling and conditional growth. The summary retains construct/input/cell-type scope; no platform, oral route or patient efficacy is inferred.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: United States, federal regulation: drug and biologic expanded access has individual-patient, intermediate-population and widespread-treatment arrangements. Criteria include serious or immediately life-threatening illness, no comparable satisfactory alternative, justified potential benefit and risk, and no interference with clinical development. A new individual-patient IND is different from a protocol under an existing active IND. Supplier agreement and applicable FDA, ethics-review and consent requirements remain separate from manufacture, institutional readiness and scheduling. Access authorization is not evidence that treatment improves outcomes.

For non-emergency individual-patient use, a new IND ordinarily becomes effective 30 calendar days after FDA receipt unless held or FDA permits earlier use. An individual-patient protocol under an existing active IND has no automatic 30-day wait, but must be submitted and have applicable IRB approval and consent. Widespread-use treatment protocols have different start rules.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: For non-emergency individual-patient use, a new IND ordinarily becomes effective 30 calendar days after FDA receipt unless held or FDA permits earlier use. An individual-patient protocol under an existing active IND has no automatic 30-day wait, but must be submitted and have applicable IRB approval and consent. Widespread-use treatment protocols have different start rules.

Emergency individual-patient use can receive prior FDA authorisation by telephone or other rapid communication, allowing use to begin before the written expanded-access submission. That submission is due within 15 working days of FDA authorisation. When there is insufficient time for prospective institutional review board (IRB) review, report the emergency use to the IRB within 5 working days of starting treatment. Subsequent use at the same institution normally requires prior IRB review. FDA's April 2026 guidance also describes discretion for a subsequent emergency request when prior review is infeasible, with the same 5-working-day reporting requirement. This is not continuing permission or a promised treatment date.
